name: Minimum Degree
definition: The **minimum degree** of a concept class is defined as the minimum degree of its $1$-inclusion graph.
graph_summary: The minimum vertex degree in the one-inclusion graph.
comments: Not c-monotonic: for $\mathcal H=\{000,001,110\}$, the isolated function $110$ makes the minimum degree $0$, while conditioning the first coordinate to $0$ leaves an edge of minimum degree $1$.

c_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: H={000,001,110} has an isolated vertex and hence minimum degree 0, while conditioning its first coordinate to 0 leaves an edge of minimum degree 1.

monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\{000,001,110\}$ has an isolated vertex and minimum degree 0, whereas its subfamily $\{000,001\}$ is an edge and has minimum degree 1.

p_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\mathcal H=\{000,001,110\}$ has minimum degree 0. Projecting to the last two coordinates gives the two-edge path $\{00,01,10\}$, whose minimum degree is 1.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.
